nodes.label: TESTING.md Manual E2E Checklist
nodes.rationale: First execution of the system: nothing in the repository had been run before, so every step is a genuine assertion, not a formality. Work top to bottom — later sections depend on data created by earlier ones. No automated tests exist; this checklist IS the entire test suite. Sections marked with a warning are the ones most likely to fail first. NOTE: this document predates several CLAUDE.md decisions and still describes the two-step unit-login flow, TKT-[A-Z2-9]{6} random numbering, and the navy/gold palette.

nodes.label: COOKIE_SAMESITE=none for Local Dev
nodes.rationale: Web (:3000) and API (:4000) are different origins locally, so a Lax cookie set by a cross-site response is never sent back and login 'succeeds' while every request after it is anonymous. Production uses lax behind a single domain. This is the root cause behind the two most common test failures: agent step 2 bouncing back to step 1, and the dashboard socket never connecting.

nodes.label: Missing .next Chunk / fuseblk Corruption
nodes.rationale: 'Cannot find module ./912.js' is NOT a stale cache you can simply delete — it means a next dev/start was left running while next build rewrote .next underneath it, so the live server serves a manifest pointing at chunks that no longer exist. Compounded by the repo living on an NTFS-3G (fuseblk) mount: FUSE cannot unlink a file another process holds open, so it renames it to .fuse_hidden<inode> and rm -rf .next then fails with 'Directory not empty', regenerating a new .fuse_hidden on every attempt. Kill the server first, then clear. Never run dev:web and build against the same .next at once — on this filesystem that reliably corrupts the chunk manifest.

nodes.label: Offline → Queue → Sync Test (§4.5)
nodes.rationale: The single most important test in the document. Verifies the green+WifiOff PENDING SYNC overlay is visually distinct from a confirmed admission, that the guest is admitted anyway (the gate never blocks), that the IndexedDB ps.scan_queue row carries client_scan_id/payload/offline_scanned_at, that a re-scan while still offline is caught by local dedupe with no network, that the queue drains within ~5s of the API returning, and that scan_logs.created_at is the CAPTURE time, not the sync time.

nodes.label: Bulk-Sync Idempotency Replay Test
nodes.rationale: Replaying a completed batch verbatim must return the ORIGINAL verdict with replay:true, and scan_logs must still hold exactly one row for that client_scan_id — the assertion behind the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING idempotency key.

nodes.label: Revoked Ticket Join Test
nodes.rationale: Scanning an unscanned guest code on a REVOKED ticket must go red, and qr_codes.status must still read ISSUED — proving the ticket JOIN inside the conditional UPDATE blocked it, not a separate pre-check that could race.

nodes.label: QR Secrecy Assertion
nodes.rationale: qr_hash must be 64 hex chars (a SHA-256), never a readable UUID, and no column anywhere may hold the raw payload. Section 3.6 therefore says to KEEP the issuance response: re-fetching payloads is impossible by design.

nodes.label: Server-Authority Attack Test
nodes.rationale: POSTing a Normal ticket with counted_persons:4 must return 400 VALIDATION_ERROR because .strict() rejects the unknown key outright, and the database must confirm no Normal ticket ever stored capacity other than 1. This is the executable form of CLAUDE.md §4.3.

nodes.label: PWA Service Worker Assertions
nodes.rationale: Requires a production build — the worker is inert in dev by design, and in dev the console logs it being unregistered. Offline reload must show the styled offline page, not the browser's dinosaur, and /api/* requests must NEVER appear as '(from ServiceWorker)' — the executable form of the shell-only scope rule.
